why_misclassified: CSPM validates technical properties of VPC peering (route tables, security groups) but does not check if the peering is documented in the ATO boundary as an authorized interconnection.
detection_signal: VPC peering connection active, route tables valid — no finding
ground_truth: Undocumented interconnection between FedRAMP and non-FedRAMP VPC — violates FedRAMP interconnection requirements (CA-3); data residency risk
remediation_impact: Non-FedRAMP system connected to FedRAMP boundary; ISSO unaware; violates System Security Plan interconnection documentation

scenario: A compliance tool flags GovCloud account root email addresses as using commercial domain email (@agency.gov) instead of government-specific email. AWS GovCloud requires .gov or .mil email addresses for root accounts — the accounts use .gov email, which IS a government domain. The tool incorrectly classifies .gov as 'commercial' rather than recognizing it as a US government domain.
why_misclassified: Tool's domain classification algorithm treats .gov as non-government because its allowlist only contains .mil — fails to recognize .gov as the primary US civilian government domain.
detection_signal: Root account email domain not in approved government domain list
ground_truth: .gov domains are US government civilian domains — exactly the correct domain for civilian agency GovCloud accounts
remediation_impact: No action needed — .gov IS the correct government domain; tool has incorrect domain classification

scenario: An Azure Government subscription has an alert suppression rule that suppresses all 'Unusual user activity' alerts to reduce noise during a major system migration. The migration completed 4 months ago but the suppression rule was never removed. Real anomalous user activity (consistent with credential theft pattern) is being suppressed and not investigated.
why_misclassified: CSPM does not audit suppression rule relevance or expiration — a valid suppression rule that should have been removed looks identical to a current justified suppression.
detection_signal: Alert suppression rule active — unusual user activity alerts suppressed, no SIEM events generated
ground_truth: Stale suppression rule from completed migration; active credential theft pattern being suppressed; 4 months of real alerts silenced
remediation_impact: Active credential compromise undetected; attacker potentially operating undetected for months inside Azure Government

scenario: SCC flags a Cloud SQL instance in GCP Assured Workloads as not requiring SSL connections. The Cloud SQL instance uses Private Service Connect — all connections originate from VNet-internal services using IAM-authenticated Cloud SQL Auth Proxy. The proxy handles TLS termination with FIPS-compliant ciphers. The ssl_mode setting on the instance itself is irrelevant when Auth Proxy is used.
why_misclassified: SSL requirement check evaluates the Cloud SQL instance ssl_mode without detecting that all connections use Auth Proxy which enforces TLS regardless of this setting.
detection_signal: Cloud SQL ssl_mode = ALLOW_UNENCRYPTED_AND_ENCRYPTED
ground_truth: All connections via Cloud SQL Auth Proxy — TLS enforced at proxy layer regardless of instance ssl_mode; FIPS-compliant ciphers used
remediation_impact: Changing ssl_mode would have no security effect since Auth Proxy is the connection intermediary

scenario: An IAM role in GovCloud was created by a developer during testing and never deleted. The role has no active sessions and no scheduled usage — but it has a trust policy allowing assumption from a contractor's external AWS account. The contractor's engagement ended 18 months ago. Access Analyzer shows no active usage and generates no finding because the role has not been used recently.
why_misclassified: IAM Access Analyzer external access findings are based on policy analysis but Access Analyzer does not flag unused roles — only active findings on externally accessible resources appear in reports.
detection_signal: No finding — role is unused, Access Analyzer shows no active external access
ground_truth: Orphaned role with external contractor trust policy — contractor may still hold AWS credentials enabling assumption; ghost access path exists
remediation_impact: Orphaned role with contractor trust policy is persistent attack vector; contractor credentials could allow GovCloud access months/years after engagement ends

scenario: Config flags CloudFormation stacks in GovCloud as having drift. The drift is an intentional tag addition on resources — an automated tagging Lambda adds FISMA-required resource tags (data-classification, ato-boundary, system-owner) to all resources after deployment. These tags are not in the CFN template but are required by FISMA compliance. The tagging Lambda is an authorized complement to CFN deployments.
why_misclassified: CFN drift detection flags any resource property not in the template including authorized post-deployment compliance tagging that enhances rather than undermines the deployment.
detection_signal: CloudFormation stack resource has properties not in template — drift detected
ground_truth: Authorized FISMA compliance tagging Lambda adds required tags post-deployment — intentional complement to CFN, not unauthorized drift
remediation_impact: Correcting drift by removing FISMA-required tags would cause compliance violations in the tagging-based compliance reports

scenario: An Azure Government tenant has PIM (Privileged Identity Management) configured for all privileged roles. A service principal has a permanent active Owner assignment bypassing PIM — service principals cannot use PIM just-in-time activation, so it was given permanent access. The service principal has overly broad Owner rights that were 'temporary' for initial setup and never scoped down.
why_misclassified: PIM reporting confirms all human user privileged roles use JIT. Service principal permanent role assignments are excluded from PIM reports — the bypass is invisible in PIM compliance dashboards.
detection_signal: PIM enabled for all user privileged roles — compliance dashboard shows green
ground_truth: Service principal with permanent Owner role bypasses JIT requirement; initial setup scope creep never cleaned up
remediation_impact: Permanent Owner SP enables persistent privilege escalation path; compromise of SP secrets grants permanent subscription Owner access

scenario: SCC flags a Cloud Run service in GCP Assured Workloads as allowing unauthenticated invocations. The Cloud Run service is the agency public API for citizen data submission — it intentionally allows unauthenticated access from the public internet so citizens can submit forms without prior registration. Business logic validates submission format; no sensitive data is returned.
why_misclassified: Unauthenticated Cloud Run access flagged as HIGH without recognizing that citizen-facing government APIs intentionally allow public access per government service delivery requirements.
detection_signal: Cloud Run service allows allUsers invocation (unauthenticated)
ground_truth: Public citizen submission API — intentionally unauthenticated to enable citizen data submissions without account requirement; no sensitive data returned
remediation_impact: Adding authentication to citizen submission API would prevent citizens from submitting required forms, blocking government service delivery

scenario: Config flags a large fleet of GovCloud EC2 instances as lacking detailed CloudWatch monitoring. The instances are CDM sensor appliances — they run on a fixed 5-minute reporting cycle aligned with the CDM program data collection schedule. Detailed 1-minute CloudWatch monitoring would provide no additional visibility beyond CDM's 5-minute cycle and doubles per-instance monitoring costs.
why_misclassified: Detailed monitoring requirement applied uniformly without considering CDM-compliant monitoring cycles that already satisfy continuous monitoring requirements.
detection_signal: EC2 instances have basic (5-min) CloudWatch monitoring instead of detailed (1-min)
ground_truth: CDM sensor appliances with 5-minute collection cycle aligned to CDM program requirements; detailed monitoring provides no operational benefit
remediation_impact: Enabling detailed monitoring on CDM sensors doubles per-instance monitoring cost with no security improvement

scenario: A GovCloud S3 bucket has Macie enabled and shows as having no sensitive data. The Macie scan completed successfully but the bucket stores encrypted CUI documents with a non-standard file extension (.cuif) — a custom format used by a legacy agency application. Macie cannot read the encrypted format and reports the bucket as containing only binary blobs with no identifiable PII/CUI.
why_misclassified: Macie cannot decrypt and analyze CUI documents in encrypted custom format — reports no findings because content is opaque to the scanner.
detection_signal: Macie scan complete, no sensitive data detected — bucket appears compliant
ground_truth: Encrypted CUI documents in custom format — Macie cannot inspect content; actual data classification is CUI requiring higher controls
remediation_impact: CUI bucket classified as non-sensitive; controls appropriate for sensitive data not applied; access controls may be insufficient

scenario: Azure Policy flags resource groups in Azure Government as lacking CanNotDelete locks. The agency uses Azure Blueprints with a built-in policy that enforces delete locks automatically on all production resource groups — the lock is applied by Blueprint assignment. The policy check looks for manually applied locks and does not detect Blueprint-managed locks as equivalent.
why_misclassified: Policy check detects manual resource locks only; Blueprint-managed locks satisfy the same control but are implemented via Blueprint mechanism not visible to the manual lock check.
detection_signal: Resource group has no direct resource lock applied
ground_truth: Azure Blueprint applies CanNotDelete lock as part of Blueprint governance — lock present but via Blueprint mechanism
remediation_impact: Manually adding locks on Blueprint-managed resources creates conflict with Blueprint lifecycle management and may cause Blueprint compliance drift

scenario: Security Hub flags an ElastiCache Redis cluster in GovCloud as lacking AUTH token. The Redis cluster is accessible only via VPC endpoint from a single application's private subnet — no other subnet has route access. The application authenticates at the application layer using HMAC signing on all Redis operations. AUTH token would add redundant auth on an already network-isolated cluster.
why_misclassified: AUTH token check applied universally without considering network isolation as a compensating control for single-consumer ElastiCache clusters.
detection_signal: ElastiCache Redis cluster auth_token not configured
ground_truth: VPC-isolated single-consumer Redis cluster with HMAC application-layer authentication; network isolation is compensating control
remediation_impact: Adding AUTH token requires coordinated changes to application configuration and Redis simultaneously — creates deployment complexity for defense-in-depth benefit that is marginal given existing isolation

scenario: A GCP Assured Workloads project has a Cloud Logging bucket with retention period configured. An admin reduced the log retention from 365 days to 30 days to reduce costs — this is a legitimate operation that GCP allows. FISMA requires 1-year audit log retention. SCC does not check logging bucket retention periods against compliance requirements.
why_misclassified: SCC validates that Cloud Logging is enabled but does not check retention period configuration against FISMA 1-year retention requirement.
detection_signal: Cloud Logging enabled — no finding generated
ground_truth: Log retention reduced to 30 days; 11 months of audit trail will not be available; violates FISMA AU-11 log retention requirements
remediation_impact: Audit logs unavailable for most of required retention period; IG audit would find FISMA non-compliance; forensic investigation capability degraded

scenario: Config flags a GovCloud Direct Connect connection as lacking a backup connection. The agency uses a dual-carrier MPLS network with automatic failover — the second carrier also terminates via Direct Connect at a different colocation facility. The backup Direct Connect exists under a different connection ID and Config evaluates each connection independently rather than as a resilient pair.
why_misclassified: Config rule checks if a single Direct Connect has a failover connection without recognizing that the failover connection exists as a separate resource with its own connection ID.
detection_signal: Primary Direct Connect connection lacks associated failover connection
ground_truth: Redundant dual-carrier Direct Connect with failover at separate colocation — Config evaluates connections independently missing the pair relationship
remediation_impact: No action needed — dual-carrier resilience exists; alert generates unnecessary engineering investigation

scenario: An Azure Government tenant has Conditional Access policies requiring CAC/PIV authentication for all enterprise applications. One Conditional Access policy has a named location exclusion for 'DISA STIG testing lab' — a range that covers 2 subnets. The STIG testing lab was decommissioned 2 years ago and the IP ranges were reallocated to a contractor's development network. The CA exclusion now exempts contractor IPs from PIV.
why_misclassified: Defender for Cloud validates CA policies are configured without checking if named location exclusions reference current and accurate IP ranges.
detection_signal: Conditional Access policy with named location configured — appears valid
ground_truth: Decommissioned location exclusion IP range reassigned to contractor — contractor can bypass PIV requirement from development network
remediation_impact: Contractor network bypasses PIV authentication; violates HSPD-12 and FedRAMP identity requirements for contractor access

scenario: Inspector V2 flags a HIGH CVE on a GovCloud EC2 instance running an internal helpdesk ticketing system for non-sensitive administrative requests. The system processes only internal IT service requests with no mission data, no PII, and no external connectivity. The HIGH severity is appropriate for mission-critical systems but this is a support tool with FISMA Low categorization.
why_misclassified: CVSS-based severity does not account for system FISMA categorization level — HIGH CVE on a FISMA Low support tool carries much lower actual risk than the same CVE on a FISMA High mission system.
detection_signal: CVE CVSS 7.8 HIGH on EC2 instance
ground_truth: FISMA Low support tool — same CVE that would be HIGH on mission system is LOW-risk in practice; no mission data, no external connectivity
remediation_impact: Emergency patch response for FISMA Low support tool competes with patching genuinely critical FISMA High systems, misallocating security resources

scenario: A DoD contractor's GovCloud environment stores CUI on EBS volumes attached to processing instances. CMMC Level 2 requires marking, sanitization, and tracking of all CUI media. EBS snapshots are created automatically by Data Lifecycle Manager on a daily schedule. The snapshots are not tagged with CUI classification markings — the DLM policy creates untagged snapshots, bypassing the CUI tagging requirement applied to the source volumes. CSPM validates that EBS volumes are tagged correctly but does not track snapshot tagging inheritance.
why_misclassified: CSPM checks resource tags on EBS volumes but does not verify that automated snapshot processes preserve required CUI classification tags. DLM-created snapshots are a separate resource type not in the tagging compliance check scope.
detection_signal: EBS volumes CUI-tagged compliant — no finding. DLM snapshot tags not evaluated.
ground_truth: DLM policy creates EBS snapshots without inheriting source volume tags. 847 snapshots containing CUI without CMMC-required classification markings. NIST SP 800-171 3.8.1 requires physical/digital media with CUI to be marked per CUI marking requirements.
remediation_impact: Untagged CUI snapshots may be shared, copied to non-CUI accounts, or retained beyond authorized periods — all CMMC MP controls depend on accurate markings to enforce.

scenario: Defender for Cloud flags an Azure Government tenant as allowing legacy authentication protocols. The 'legacy auth' alert fires because a Conditional Access policy has a named exclusion for the agency's SCADA monitoring systems that use NTLM authentication — these industrial control systems cannot be updated to modern auth. The SCADA systems monitor critical physical infrastructure and cannot be taken offline for authentication upgrades. A compensating control (MPLS-isolated network segment) prevents lateral movement.
why_misclassified: EC-14 legacy metadata: The finding identifies legacy auth enablement without recognizing the documented compensating control (MPLS network isolation) for SCADA systems that cannot support modern authentication protocols.
detection_signal: Conditional Access policy allows legacy authentication for service group SCADA-Legacy-Systems
ground_truth: SCADA systems on isolated MPLS segment with no internet connectivity. Legacy auth exclusion applies only to systems at IP ranges on the dedicated SCADA VLAN. ISSO-approved compensating control documented in SSP Section 3.4.
remediation_impact: Blocking legacy auth for SCADA systems would disable monitoring of critical infrastructure — potential public safety and mission impact.

scenario: A DoD contractor's GCP Assured Workloads project stores ITAR-controlled technical data in a BigQuery dataset in us-east4. A data transfer job was created to replicate analysis results to a BigQuery dataset in europe-west2 for a joint project with a UK partner. The transfer job was created by a data engineer who was unaware of ITAR export control restrictions. GCP SCC reports the Assured Workloads project as compliant — it validates the primary dataset location but does not audit BigQuery Transfer Service jobs for cross-border data movements.
why_misclassified: SCC validates Assured Workloads data location controls on the primary dataset. BigQuery Transfer Service jobs are a separate resource type that can move data outside the Assured Workloads boundary without triggering compliance alerts.
detection_signal: Assured Workloads project compliant. BigQuery Transfer Service job not in scope of Assured Workloads location policy enforcement.
ground_truth: BigQuery Transfer Service job transferring ITAR-controlled technical specifications to europe-west2. UK partner access constitutes an ITAR export without State Department license. DoD contractor ITAR violation.
remediation_impact: Unauthorized ITAR export to foreign national — criminal penalties under 22 U.S.C. 2778; DoD contract termination risk; reputational and licensing consequences.

scenario: Security Hub flags an S3 bucket in a CJIS-scoped GovCloud account as having cross-account access to another AWS account. The cross-account access is to the agency's centralized audit account, which is the designated recipient for all CloudTrail logs, Config snapshots, and Security Hub findings across all agency accounts. Cross-account write to the audit account is required by the FISMA continuous monitoring architecture.
why_misclassified: EC-08 intentional cross-account access: Cross-account S3 bucket policy flagged without recognizing the FISMA-required architecture where all accounts write to a centralized immutable audit account.
detection_signal: S3 bucket policy allows s3:PutObject from external account 111122223333
ground_truth: Account 111122223333 is the agency's centralized audit account (documented in network diagram section 4.2 of the SSP). Cross-account write is the FISMA continuous monitoring required architecture for immutable audit log aggregation.
remediation_impact: Removing cross-account access would break centralized audit log delivery — FISMA continuous monitoring requirement and ATO condition would be violated.

scenario: GovCloud EC2 instances in a DoD contractor's IL4 environment passed STIG compliance scanning 6 months ago. Security Hub shows no active findings because the last STIG assessment passed. However, since the assessment, the OS was patched (RHEL 8.8 to 8.9), new packages were installed by application teams, and sshd_config was modified to re-enable PasswordAuthentication for a legacy integration. The compliance check does not run continuously — it was run once and the passing result is cached.
why_misclassified: CSPM compliance posture is based on the last scan result, not continuous state. STIG compliance that passed 6 months ago is shown as compliant even though configuration drift has occurred since the assessment.
detection_signal: Last STIG assessment: PASS (6 months ago). No continuous drift detection for STIG controls. Security Hub shows no findings.
ground_truth: sshd_config PasswordAuthentication=yes (STIG V-230369 violation). RHEL 8.9 introduced new STIG findings not present in 8.8 baseline. 3 new packages have known vulnerabilities. Cached compliance state 6 months stale.
remediation_impact: SSH password authentication enabled on IL4 systems — brute force attack vector; STIG V-230369 violation; DoD CC SRG IL4 requirement for key-only authentication violated.

scenario: GCP SCC recommends enabling Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) on an internal government application backend. The application is an internal HR system accessible only via the agency's MPLS network through a Dedicated Interconnect. The application already uses PIV/CAC authentication via an on-premises identity provider federating to GCP via SAML. IAP would add a redundant authentication layer that conflicts with the existing PIV authentication flow.
why_misclassified: IAP recommendation applied to all web applications without recognizing that the application is not internet-accessible and already has stronger authentication (PIV/CAC) than IAP would provide.
detection_signal: Backend service has no IAP configuration
ground_truth: Internal application on dedicated MPLS interconnect. PIV/CAC SAML federation for authentication (FIPS 201 compliant). Internet-inaccessible. IAP would introduce Google identity requirements incompatible with PIV-only agency policy.
remediation_impact: Enabling IAP on a PIV-only application would require Google identity enrollment for all agency staff — violating HSPD-12 PIV-only authentication policy.

scenario: A Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) tenant in Azure Government has guest accounts from a contractor organization with Global Administrator role assignments — granted during an emergency support engagement 11 months ago. Defender for Cloud validates that Privileged Identity Management (PIM) is configured and that Global Admins use PIM for just-in-time activation. The guests have permanent PIM-eligible assignments but their contractor organization's Conditional Access policies are weaker than the agency's — guests bypass the agency's PIV requirement via B2B federation.
why_misclassified: Defender validates PIM configuration without checking the authentication strength of federated guest accounts. B2B guest accounts are subject to the home tenant's CA policies, not the agency's PIV enforcement.
detection_signal: PIM configured, Global Admin role requires activation, JIT access enabled — compliance pass
ground_truth: Guest contractor accounts use home-tenant password+MFA (not PIV). PIM activation requires only home-tenant MFA. Guest GA accounts bypass agency PIV requirement through B2B federation — violating HSPD-12 PIV-for-privileged-access requirement.
remediation_impact: Contractor global admins can activate GA role with password+TOTP — weaker than agency PIV requirement. Credential compromise of contractor account yields full Azure Government tenant control.

scenario: GuardDuty fires a HIGH finding for Trojan:EC2/DNSDataExfiltration on a GovCloud EC2 instance. The instance is a CISA CDM (Continuous Diagnostics and Mitigation) sensor — its primary function is to send asset telemetry to the CISA CDM Dashboard via DNS-based data channels as part of its authorized operation. The high-volume DNS telemetry is flagged as exfiltration by GuardDuty's behavioral model.
why_misclassified: EC-22 security tooling: CDM sensors use DNS-based telemetry channels that are behaviorally identical to DNS tunneling for exfiltration. GuardDuty cannot distinguish authorized CDM telemetry from malicious DNS exfiltration.
detection_signal: GuardDuty: Trojan:EC2/DNSDataExfiltration — high DNS query volume with long subdomain strings to cdm.cisa.gov endpoints
ground_truth: EC2 instance is CISA CDM sensor authorized to send asset telemetry to cdm.cisa.gov. DNS telemetry is the CDM program's designated communication channel. CISA CDM documentation specifies DNS-based data delivery. GuardDuty suppression for CDM sensor IPs required.
remediation_impact: Isolating the CDM sensor breaks CISA's continuous monitoring of the agency — FISMA continuous monitoring requirement and CyberEO requirements for CISA visibility violated.

scenario: An agency's GovCloud AWS Config is enabled and collecting all resource configurations. Security Hub compliance score is 94%. However, an EC2 fleet was deployed using AWS Capacity Reservations — a launch mechanism that provisions instances under a reservation ID rather than directly. These instances appear in EC2 but are not discovered by AWS Config because Config's EC2 rule targets aws_instance resources, not instances created through the Capacity Reservation fleet mechanism. 47 production instances are not in the CMDB.
why_misclassified: AWS Config evaluates standard EC2 instance resources but Capacity Reservation fleet instances use a different provisioning path that bypasses Config's resource discovery for the fleet management layer.
detection_signal: AWS Config coverage: 94% (high score). EC2 fleet instances not visible to Config rules.
ground_truth: 47 EC2 instances deployed via Capacity Reservation fleet running production government workloads. Not in Config, not in FISMA System Security Plan resource inventory, not patched by SSM (also not discovered). NIST 800-53 CM-8 requires complete system component inventory.
remediation_impact: 47 production instances outside Config coverage, SSM patch management, and FISMA SSP inventory — unpatched, unmonitored, undocumented mission systems.

scenario: Defender for Cloud flags a Microsoft Sentinel data connector as disabled in an Azure Government production environment. The Azure AD (Entra ID) data connector was disabled for 6 hours during a Sentinel workspace migration to a new Log Analytics workspace in a different region to comply with a new data residency directive. The migration is a one-time approved change with a 6-hour maintenance window, after which the connector was re-enabled. The CSPM captured the disabled state during the maintenance window.
why_misclassified: EC-28 approved maintenance window: Sentinel data connector disabled during a documented, approved migration window is indistinguishable to CSPM from unauthorized connector disablement.
detection_signal: Microsoft Sentinel AAD data connector state=Disabled during change window
ground_truth: Approved migration change RFC-2024-0087 (Sentinel workspace migration us-east to us-gov-east for FISMA data residency). Connector disabled 02:00-08:00 UTC. Re-enabled on schedule. Change ticket documents 6-hour SIEM gap in audit trail.
remediation_impact: No action required — connector re-enabled per change plan. Automated alert generated during documented maintenance window; investigation consumes analyst time needlessly.
